title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #1

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A sweet potato vine cutting grows roots and becomes a new plant. Which sign of life is shown? (1 mark)
   A. Dying
   B. Removing waste
   C. Breathing out
   D. Reproducing

2. What are the two main types of things carried by the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Sound and light
   B. Air and stones
   C. Water and food
   D. Heat and cold

3. Which of these is a root that we eat? (1 mark)
   A. Cabbage
   B. Banana
   C. Maize grain
   D. Carrot

4. Which sign of life is shown when a yellow leaf falls from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing in
   B. Making fruit
   C. Reproducing
   D. Removing waste

5. Which of these shows a plant reproducing? (1 mark)
   A. A leaf turning green
   B. A stem getting taller
   C. A root drinking water
   D. A bean plant making pods with seeds

6. A plant on a windowsill grows towards the window. What is it responding to? (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Light
   C. Wind speed
   D. Soil colour

7. Why is a spider NOT an insect? (1 mark)
   A. It has eight legs, not six
   B. It has a backbone
   C. It has feathers
   D. It lives in water

8. Which group of animals has dry, scaly skin and includes snakes and crocodiles? (1 mark)
   A. Amphibians
   B. Mammals
   C. Birds
   D. Reptiles

9. What do vertebrates have inside their bodies that invertebrates do not? (1 mark)
   A. Six legs
   B. A backbone
   C. A shell
   D. Feathers

10. What is the waste passed out by animals called? (1 mark)
   A. Urine and faeces
   B. Milk
   C. Seeds
   D. Food

11. Which of these is NOT an animal? (1 mark)
   A. A cow
   B. A housefly
   C. A wooden toy horse
   D. A tilapia

12. A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. Which sign of life does this best show? (1 mark)
   A. Growing
   B. Dying
   C. Breathing out
   D. Feeding only

13. Which of these parts is found before the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Large intestine
   C. Rectum
   D. Gullet

14. Which of these is true about the small intestine? (1 mark)
   A. It stores faeces
   B. It swallows food
   C. It chews food
   D. Digested food passes through its wall into the blood

15. What is absorption? (1 mark)
   A. Swallowing food
   B. Digested food passing into the blood
   C. Chewing food
   D. Passing faeces

16. What can help a child with diarrhoea while waiting to see a health worker? (1 mark)
   A. Eating unwashed fruit
   B. Drinking clean water and ORS as advised
   C. Drinking dirty water
   D. Eating only sweets

17. Why is air matter? (1 mark)
   A. It is invisible
   B. It is cold
   C. It is light
   D. It has mass and takes up space

18. Which of these is a liquid used as fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Paraffin
   B. Firewood
   C. Air
   D. Charcoal

19. Which of these do we measure using litres? (1 mark)
   A. Time of a race
   B. Mass of a book
   C. Length of a rope
   D. Volume of juice

20. Which is the best way to manage the food remains from the school kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them in a river
   B. Bury plastic with them
   C. Put them in a compost pit
   D. Burn them near classrooms

21. What is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Dirty water
   B. Air from a tyre
   C. Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   D. Smoke from a fire

22. Which waste goes into a compost pit? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Plastic bags
   C. Vegetable peelings
   D. Tins

23. Which of these is NOT a way of managing solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing it in a river
   B. Composting
   C. Reusing
   D. Recycling

24. Which of these makes a good compost mixture? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   B. Glass and metal
   C. Plastic and tins
   D. Batteries and plastic

25. Which of these can make a river dry up? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   B. Using rain tanks
   C. Saving water
   D. Planting trees

26. When is the best time to water plants? (1 mark)
   A. Noon
   B. Midday only
   C. Early morning or evening
   D. Never

27. A school wastes 20 litres a day through leaks. How much in 5 days? (1 mark)
   A. 100 litres
   B. 15 litres
   C. 4 litres
   D. 25 litres

28. Which of these is a problem caused by friction? (1 mark)
   A. Lighting a match
   B. Braking a bicycle
   C. Walking safely
   D. Wearing away of shoes and tyres

29. Which of these is a pull? (1 mark)
   A. Pressing a bell
   B. Closing a door by pushing
   C. Opening a drawer by its handle
   D. Kicking a ball

30. What does a force do when it squeezes a sponge? (1 mark)
   A. Makes it lighter
   B. Changes its shape
   C. Makes it hot
   D. Changes its colour

31. What is one benefit of using translucent roof sheets in a house? (1 mark)
   A. It blocks the sun completely
   B. It makes the house dark
   C. It uses more electricity
   D. It saves electricity in the day

32. Which small living thing makes its own light and so is a natural source? (1 mark)
   A. Electric bulb
   B. Torch
   C. Firefly
   D. Candle

33. Which of these is a way of making a room lighter during the day? (1 mark)
   A. Closing the window
   B. Opening the curtains
   C. Closing the door
   D. Painting the walls black

34. What does light help us to do? (1 mark)
   A. Taste
   B. Hear
   C. Smell
   D. See

35. You want to see if a material is opaque. What do you do? (1 mark)
   A. Smell it
   B. Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   C. Weigh it
   D. Taste it

36. A flash of light in the sky during a storm is a natural source of light. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A solar lamp
   B. A car headlight
   C. A lantern
   D. Lightning

37. Which of these is opaque? (1 mark)
   A. Clear plastic
   B. Clean water
   C. Clear glass
   D. Wood

38. Which wall colour helps a room to be brighter? (1 mark)
   A. Light colours
   B. Dark brown
   C. Dark blue
   D. Dark black

39. Which battery-powered device gives artificial light? (1 mark)
   A. Torch
   B. Stars
   C. Sun
   D. Firefly

40. If you smell gas from a cooker, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Tell an adult and keep flames away
   B. Turn on an electric switch
   C. Ignore it
   D. Light a match

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain how wet clothes dry in the sun. (3 marks)

42. A ball is at rest. Kelvin kicks it, then Mercy stops it with her foot, then she kicks it to the right. Name the effect of the force in each case. (3 marks)

43. Describe the natural and artificial sources of light and explain the difference. (5 marks)

44. State three things that plants give to people. (3 marks)

45. Explain why friction can be both useful and a problem. Give two examples of each. (4 marks)

46. Sort into decomposable and non-decomposable: egg shells, tin can, cotton cloth, polythene bag, cow dung, glass bottle. (4 marks)

47. Give two ways in which animals are different from plants. (2 marks)

48. Give three safety measures to observe when cooking. (3 marks)

49. Explain why a football is described as a container of matter although it looks empty. (3 marks)

50. List the five groups of vertebrates and give one example of each. (3 marks)

51. Give three ways of lighting a house at night. (3 marks)

52. Name the three Rs of waste management. (2 marks)

53. Name the three states of matter and give one example of each. (2 marks)

54. Describe four effects of forces using examples from daily life. (4 marks)

55. Explain why a rainwater tank should have a lid. (3 marks)

56. Explain how light helps in security and safety. Give three examples. (3 marks)

57. Give three examples where a force holds objects together. (3 marks)

58. State two jobs of the mouth in digestion. (2 marks)

59. State three things a child should do when he has diarrhoea. (3 marks)

60. What is meant by water conservation? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Reproducing
   Making a new plant from part of an old plant is reproduction.

2. C — Water and food
   The stem carries water and mineral salts up and food made in leaves to other parts.

3. D — Carrot
   A carrot is a storage root. Cabbage is leaves, banana is a fruit and maize grain is a seed.

4. D — Removing waste
   Old leaves may carry waste away when they fall.

5. D — A bean plant making pods with seeds
   Making seeds is reproduction. Growing taller is growth.

6. B — Light
   Plants bend and grow towards light coming from one side.

7. A — It has eight legs, not six
   Insects have six legs and spiders have eight.

8. D — Reptiles
   Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

9. B — A backbone
   A backbone is the feature that defines vertebrates.

10. A — Urine and faeces
   Animals remove waste such as urine and faeces.

11. C — A wooden toy horse
   A toy is not alive. It does not feed, grow or reproduce.

12. A — Growing
   A caterpillar grows and changes form to become a butterfly.

13. D — Gullet
   Food passes through the gullet before it reaches the stomach.

14. D — Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   Absorption takes place there.

15. B — Digested food passing into the blood
   Absorption means digested food parts pass into the blood.

16. B — Drinking clean water and ORS as advised
   Water and ORS replace what the body loses.

17. D — It has mass and takes up space
   Air fills balloons and pushes against things, so it takes up space.

18. A — Paraffin
   Paraffin and petrol are liquid fuels.

19. D — Volume of juice
   Litres measure volume.

20. C — Put them in a compost pit
   Kitchen waste can be composted.

21. C — Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   Solid waste is unwanted solid material.

22. C — Vegetable peelings
   Only decomposable waste is composted.

23. A — Throwing it in a river
   Throwing waste in rivers pollutes water.

24. A — Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   Composting uses natural plant waste.

25. A — Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   Cutting trees near sources reduces water.

26. C — Early morning or evening
   Less water evaporates when it is cooler.

27. A — 100 litres
   20 x 5 = 100 litres.

28. D — Wearing away of shoes and tyres
   Friction wears surfaces away.

29. C — Opening a drawer by its handle
   A handle is pulled toward you.

30. B — Changes its shape
   Squeezing changes the shape.

31. D — It saves electricity in the day
   Daylight comes in so lamps are not needed.

32. C — Firefly
   Fireflies make their own light.

33. B — Opening the curtains
   Open curtains let in more daylight.

34. D — See
   Light lets us see objects.

35. B — Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   If no light passes, it is opaque.

36. D — Lightning
   Lightning is a natural flash of light.

37. D — Wood
   Wood blocks light.

38. A — Light colours
   Light colours reflect more light.

39. A — Torch
   A torch is made by people.

40. A — Tell an adult and keep flames away
   Gas can catch fire, so avoid flames.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Heat from the sun makes the water evaporate. It changes to vapour and goes into the air so the clothes become dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sun heat, 1 mark for evaporation, 1 mark for the result.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kelvin starts motion, Mercy stops motion, Mercy's second kick changes direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct effect.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Natural sources are found in nature such as the sun, stars, lightning and fireflies. Artificial sources are made by people such as bulbs, torches and candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for natural and artificial, 1 mark for examples of each and 1 mark for the difference.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Food, shade, wood, medicine, clean air (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Useful: brakes stop bicycles and shoes grip the ground. A problem: it wears out tyres and makes machines hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it helps in some cases and harms in others, and 1 mark for each correct example up to 3.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: egg shells, cotton cloth, cow dung. Non-decomposable: tin can, polythene bag, glass bottle.
   Working / marking points: Award 4 marks for all correct, 3 for five, 2 for four and 1 for three.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Animals can move from place to place. Animals feed on ready-made food while plants make their own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct difference.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use gloves, turn handles inwards, keep children away, do not play with matches, keep paraffin away from fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is full of air. Air is a gas, so it has mass and takes up space. It keeps the ball in shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air being matter, 1 mark for it filling the ball.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mammals (goat), birds (hen), reptiles (snake), amphibians (frog), fish (tilapia).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct five groups, 1 mark for four examples, 1 mark for correct matching.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric bulbs, solar lamps, paraffin lamps, candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Solid (stone), liquid (water), gas (air).
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for the three states and 1 mark for correct examples.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: A force changes the shape of dough, starts a ball moving, stops a bicycle with brakes and changes the direction of a ball when hit with a stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect with an example.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps out dirt and leaves and stops mosquitoes from breeding in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for mosquitoes, 1 mark for making water safer.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Street lights help people see, security lights keep thieves away, traffic lights direct drivers, torches show dangers, reflectors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Glue holding paper, nails holding wood, rope tying things, stitches holding cloth, screws.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Teeth cut and grind food. The tongue moves food and saliva wets it and starts digesting starch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct job.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tell an adult, drink clean water or ORS, and see a health worker. Keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Using water carefully and protecting water sources so that there is enough for everyone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for careful use and 1 mark for protecting or enough for everyone.
